Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1356.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Pu’an Yinsu. Pu'an Yinsu owns the retained deployment: teaches that the buddha sees the beings' world as owning no name or surname, no male or female face, nothing at all, the one nature that owns no nature shining through past and present, bare and alone with not a hair's breadth of gap, while beings refuse to own it and take it on straight.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB202.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi. Baichi Xingyuan owns the retained deployment: at the lantern festival sets the silver blossoms flaring in the short lanes and long streets and the strolling lads and dancing girls treading songs into the clouds against a light clearly shining through past and present and distinctly outpassing sound and form, needing no Wenchu at the east of the blessed city nor the tower gate opening to meet Maitreya.

Senses.Explanation: One light run across all time, and the masters who claim it and then outrun it. Yuanwu Keqin at the state-opening of the great monastery under imperial decree calls the whole rite one buddha-work shining through past and present, with the prefect's banners arriving and ten thousand households singing, Pu'an Yinsu teaches that the single nature, owning no nature, shines through past and present, bare and alone, with not a hair's breadth of gap, yet beings refuse to claim it, Liao'an Qingyu verses the Way-man's light as neither small nor great, shining through past and present in an unending night, after the nine suns are shot down, and Feiyin Tongrong sets pearl sunk in the sea and sword buried in ruins against the step above the crown of the head in everyone, the school that outruns buddha and patriarch, shining through past and present beyond seeing and hearing. Wanru Tongwei holds the one word neither forward nor back that the buddhas of the three times cannot gloss nor the patriarchs of the ages lift, needing to cover heaven and earth and shine through past and present with the true eye open, Yinyuan Longqi parts one thread of a way with his whisk raised so the light fills heaven and mirrors earth, shines through past and present, and runs eight ways open on this side and the far shore, Baiyu Jingsi chants no buddha-way above to attain, no beings below to save, a light no sun or sea can figure, shining through past and present, self-complete without fabrication, and Baichi Xingyuan at the lantern festival sets the silver blooms of the short lanes and long streets against a light clearly shining through past and present and distinctly outpassing sound and form.
